messages:
pagerbot: INCIDENT detected — sustained 5xx spike for Redwood-Dedicated pool `dp1` (us-west-2). error_rate: 18% over 5m, target <0.5%. Paging oncall team. :rotating_light:
Maya P.: seeing it, HTML requests especially. Looks tied to a sudden traffic surge from partner-prod.
Ajay R.: confirmed. metrics: RPS up 3.5x, avg latency up 300ms, CUDA queue length jumping.
Dina K.: are we hitting the pool autoscale ceiling? which pool config?
Tom L.: dp1 is Dedicated-Standard, min_nodes=4, max_nodes=16, burst_disabled=false, current_nodes=16. Autoscaler logs show throttle at scale_up because of quota on tenant GPUs.
Evelyn S.: hmm. Customer-facing impact: a subset of customers on dedicated plan report timeouts. Not platform-wide but high severity for those tenants.
Maya P.: mitigation options: 1) toggle burst capacity to allow +50% for next 15m 2) enforce temporary per-tenant rate limits 3) disable heavy features (llm-streaming for dp1) 4) fallback routing to hosted models for non-sensitive tenants.
Ajay R.: can we toggle burst now? I can flip if we agree. Paging the infra-sre runbook: @oncall-rotation do we have approvals for auto-burst?
oncall-rotation: you have approval for emergency burst up to +100% for up to 30m. Log actions in incident channel.
Dina K.: we should do burst +50% immediately then assess. If error rate drops -> thumbs up. If not, escalate to throttling.
Maya P.: agreed. Ajay, run: `/infra toggle-burst dp1 --percent 50 --duration 15m --reason "traffic surge partner-prod"`
Ajay R.: running now...
pagerbot: Command executed: `/infra toggle-burst dp1 --percent 50 --duration 15m` by Ajay R. New effective max_nodes=24 (soft). Action id: ACT-2837-01.
Tom L.: kernel: watching queue. If queuing persists, we'll need to change batching config or temporarily lower `max_context_len` for non-enterprise tenants.
Evelyn S.: notifying affected customers: sending a short heads-up to partner-prod and enterprise buyers.
Maya P.: within 90s I see reduced CUDA queue length and latency dropping ~120ms. error_rate down from 18% -> 6% in 3m. Good sign.
Ajay R.: monitoring autoscaler logs: scale events allowed, nodes provisioning. Burst usage at 40% of allowance.
Dina K.: let's set a protective per-tenant token bucket for partner-prod: 1200 rps -> 900 rps for next 20m to protect remaining tenants.
Maya P.: can you apply rate limit quickly? Command: `/ratelimit apply --tenant partner-prod --qps 900 --duration 20m --scope dp1`
Ajay R.: applied. Rule id RL-2837-21. Pager: customers behind the partner-prod subflow should see reduced throughput but more reliable responses.
Evelyn S.: partner-prod acknowledges, they can queue some offline jobs. Thanks.
Tom L.: rebuild check: a couple of worker pods failed to attach KV cache during node add; that's likely why some requests still 500. I'm restarting the cache-attach daemon on new nodes.
pagerbot: oncall handover scheduled: night -> day in 12m. Maya P. will hand off to Evelyn S. after incident stabilizes.
Maya P.: quick status for handoff: burst +50% active (ends in 8m), RL applied to partner-prod, error_rate trending down to 4.5%. Ongoing task: watch KV-attach restarts and ensure no cache miss storms.
Evelyn S.: taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring for 30m and prepare rollback plan.
Ajay R.: note: if error_rate doesn't fall under 1% after burst ends, next step is temporary feature gating: `llm-streaming=false` for dp1 for non-enterprise tenants. That reduces avg token output by ~30% but lowers compute per-request.
Dina K.: logging mitigation decisions in incident tracker: https://internal.redwood/incidents/2837 (created).
Maya P.: also created a quick eval to compare generated token counts vs CPU usage: attached snippet in case we need to tune smart-batching.
Maya P.: ```
# quick check CPU vs tokens
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) as minute, sum(cpu_ms) as cpu, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM model_requests
WHERE pool='dp1' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute DESC;
```
Ajay R.: good. I see heavy token churn at the same minute the partner job spikes. Could sandbox them later.
Evelyn S.: burst expires in 5m. plan: if error_rate < 2% at expiry, we drop burst and keep RL for another 10m. if >2% -> extend burst + option to increase to +100% (requires exec approval).
pagerbot: Reminder: file incident postmortem draft in 24h and ping SRE + Platform leads.
Tom L.: cache-attach daemon restart completed on 3 nodes. no errors in logs. KV miss rate returning to baseline.
Maya P.: error_rate at 1.8% now. latency stable. Good.
Evelyn S.: burst expired, system holding. error_rate 1.3%. I'm removing the temporary rate limit in 10m unless we see regression.
Ajay R.: RL removal command: `/ratelimit remove RL-2837-21` -> executed.
pagerbot: Action completed: RL-2837-21 removed.
Evelyn S.: removing burst doesn't require a command, it was time-limited. nodes scaling back gracefully.
Dina K.: final notes for handoff closure: root cause likely a correlated heavy batch job from partner-prod combined with cache-attach delays on scale-out. Mitigations used: emergency burst, per-tenant RL, cache restarts. Follow-ups: 1) increase burst quota for dp1 permanently? 2) harden cache attach on node-provision path 3) impose soft per-tenant burst protection to avoid single tenant stomping.
Maya P.: filing follow-ups assigned to infra-sre and platform capacity planning.
Evelyn S.: closing handoff. Will prepare short incident summary for customers. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
